papers.title: Aperiodic dynamics track cortical state shifts during sleep K-complexes.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Time-resolved spectral parameterization of overnight sleep EEG distinguished genuine aperiodic shifts from waveform artifacts around expert-annotated K-complexes, and a component of the K-complex-locked change in aperiodic exponent survived controls, indicating a transient shift toward a higher-exponent, inhibition-dominated cortical state.

papers.title: The development of slow and fast theta oscillations in the human brain.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using intracranial EEG from 101 children and adults across task-based and resting-state conditions, the study revealed distinct slow and fast theta oscillations in all sampled brain regions, with a spatial gradient where slow theta speeds up and fast theta slows down from posterior to anterior regions; the dissociation peaked in young adulthood, and individual differences in task-based slow theta frequencies in hippocampus and prefrontal cortex predicted memory performance.

papers.title: All Roads Lead to Rome: Resting-State Criticality as a Neurophysiological Marker of Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) Performance in People with Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) and Healthy Participants.
papers.summary: This exploratory study related resting-state EEG criticality measures to subsequent brain-computer interface performance in people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and healthy participants, finding that neuronal avalanche dynamics, spectral slope, and Lempel-Ziv complexity consistently correlated with BCI performance in ALS but showed inverted correlation patterns in healthy participants; the authors proposed the B-ARC framework positing an inverted U-shaped relationship between proximity to criticality and BCI control.

papers.title: LTPat-based SOXFE: A self-organized explainable feature engineering model for automated fibromyalgia detection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: This study evaluated a self-organized explainable feature engineering (SOXFE) model using LTPat feature extraction, CWNCA selection, tkNN classification, and DLob explanation for EEG-based fibromyalgia detection from sleep EEG in NREM stage 2 and stage 3. Record-wise LORO yielded held-out-epoch accuracy of 92.77% for stage 2 and 97.00% for stage 3, but participant linkage was unavailable, so person-independent performance may be overestimated.

papers.title: Combined population and patient-specific brain networks predict electrical stimulation propagation.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Using single-pulse stimulation data from 34 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing stereo-EEG monitoring, the authors developed interpretable multimodal models integrating normative and patient-specific features to predict cortico-cortical evoked potential responses, achieving a median AUC of 0.84; feature relevance varied with spatial scale, and prediction errors were significantly higher within seizure onset zones.

papers.title: The EEG multi-scale brain network and high-order synergy changes in disorders of consciousness during general anesthesia.
papers.summary: EEG from 33 patients with disorders of consciousness during general anesthesia was analyzed with a multi-scale brain network framework combining minimum spanning tree, directed phase lag index, topological data analysis, and high-order mutual information; unresponsive wakefulness syndrome patients showed fragmented topology, impaired prefrontal top-down communication, reduced topological resilience, and increased redundant information processing, while minimally conscious state patients showed transient disruption and recovery of frontoparietal organization and restored synergistic integration.

papers.title: A Multi-Domain EEG Framework Integrating Spectral, Functional Connectivity, and Topological Features for Subject-Level ADHD Classification
papers.summary: The study developed an EEG classification framework for subject-level ADHD diagnosis by integrating spectral, functional connectivity (wPLI), and topological (persistent homology) features. Using SVM after recursive feature elimination, it achieved 80.17% accuracy and 86.72% ROC-AUC, with ablation showing multi-domain fusion outperformed single domains and explainable AI highlighting functional connectivity as the primary contributor.

papers.title: An adaptive, variable-length test for certifying electroencephalographic spike-detection skill: A retrospective feasibility study.
papers.summary: This retrospective feasibility study modeled EEG spike-detection skill using signal-detection parameters (discrimination σ and bias t) and evaluated an adaptive, variable-length test for certifying readers. The adaptive test preserved skill-tier ordering (experts 100% pass, novices 14%) and reliably estimated skill with a median of ~95 trials for passing experts and ~20 for clear failures, demonstrating a scalable competency assessment method.

papers.title: What drives intersubject correlation of EEG during auditory narratives?
papers.summary: The study investigated the drivers of intersubject correlation (ISC) of EEG during auditory narratives using temporal response functions (TRFs) and correlated component analysis. Acoustic features explained more variance and were main contributors to ISC, while word surprisal affected ISC only during active engagement, and linear responses accounted for only a small fraction of ISC, suggesting nonlinear responses dominate.

papers.title: Synchronized audiovisual stimulation enhances neural entrainment: convergent evidence from complementary EEG biomarkers.
papers.summary: The study investigated how synchronized audiovisual stimulation (visual flicker plus binaural beats) modulates EEG neural entrainment at 8, 20, and 40 Hz using spectral, complexity, phase-locking, and IRASA measures. Adding binaural beats enhanced periodic SSVEP components at 8 and 20 Hz and at 40 Hz increased aperiodic offset and exponent without significant periodic modulation, showing frequency-dependent spectral reorganization through complementary biomarkers.

papers.title: Social attention and coordinated movement produce dissociable spectral and network changes during dyadic improvisational dance.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using dual-brain mobile EEG during dyadic improvisational dance, the study dissociated spectral and network changes associated with social attention, verbal engagement, and coordinated movement. Nonverbal social attention flattened the aperiodic exponent and desynchronized alpha, verbal engagement added high-frequency amplitude coupling, and coordinated movement decreased theta/alpha coupling in frontoparietal control networks; four weeks of dance training increased empathic responsiveness (g = 0.82).

papers.title: Enhanced cortical tracking of unfamiliar languages in both monolinguals and bilinguals.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The study used EEG and temporal response function (TRF) modeling to examine cortical tracking of continuous speech in monolingual and bilingual adults listening to familiar and unfamiliar languages. Both groups showed enhanced tracking for unfamiliar relative to familiar languages, and bilinguals showed stronger overall cortical tracking than monolinguals across all languages, suggesting bilingual experience alters neural speech encoding.

papers.title: Transcranial magneto-acoustic stimulation modulates M1-PPN spike-LFP coupling and improves motor dysfunction in parkinsonian rats.
papers.summary: In Parkinsonian rats, transcranial magneto-acoustic stimulation (TMAS) improved motor performance and increased SNc TH-positive cells, with M1-PPN spike-LFP coherence and phase-locking changes that varied by frequency band, behavioral state, and putative neuronal class.

papers.title: Intracranial characterization of gamma in humans in response to auditory gratings
papers.summary: Intracranial recordings in seven epilepsy patients during auditory grating presentation showed a transient broadband gamma increase (30-100 Hz) followed by sustained beta suppression (14-28 Hz), with gamma selective for slower spectro-temporal modulations.

papers.title: Modulation of the speed of Intrinsic Alpha Frequency (IAF) with tACS modulates variability of illusory speech perception
papers.summary: Using tACS at intrinsic alpha frequency and ±2 Hz offsets over occipital electrodes in 27 healthy participants, this study found that tACS significantly reduced illusory /ta/ percepts in McGurk trials and that a Kuramoto-oscillator model explained the percentage of illusory responses.

papers.title: Brief Trains of Closed-loop TMS Induce Controllable Power in FM-theta Oscillations
papers.summary: This study locked brief rhythmic TMS trains to real-time frontal-midline theta phase in six healthy adults and found that trough-triggered, but not peak-triggered, trains transiently increased post-train FM-theta power (4.6-7.1 Hz) about 50-440 ms after stimulation, without affecting task performance.

papers.title: A touch that lingers: synchronized patting strengthens neural tracking of auditory rhythm in newborns
papers.summary: In 40 full-term newborns, high-density EEG showed that neural tracking of French lullabies was stronger when songs were accompanied by synchronized patting, and this enhancement persisted during subsequent periods without touch, especially in newborns with weaker auditory-only tracking.

papers.title: Pre-treatment EEG microstates and response to antipsychotic drugs in first episode psychosis.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In 56 minimally treated first-episode psychosis patients, baseline EEG microstate PC1 predicted 12-week antipsychotic treatment response (adjusted OR=0.63, AUC=72.3% with clinical information), and results were stable when PC1 weights were derived from an independent healthy control dataset.

papers.title: Prefrontal EEG Delta-Beta Coupling Marks Depressed State in Adult Siblings.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Resting-state EEG delta-beta phase-amplitude coupling was elevated over left-medial frontal regions in individuals with current MDD relative to their unaffected siblings, but not in remitted-MDD families, indicating that this coupling reflects a depressive state rather than a trait-like vulnerability.

papers.title: Hyperexcitable but seizure-free: hippocampal network dysfunction in a Wolfram syndrome model.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Characterized hippocampal function in mice carrying a patient-orthologous Wfs1 p.W542* variant, finding that dissociated hippocampal neurons were hyperexcitable but showed no increased network bursting or shift in criticality, and in vivo EEG showed no seizures despite male-specific reductions in low-gamma power and impaired fear memory. Proposes that cellular hyperexcitability does not translate into network bursting, potentially due to disproportionate loss of excitatory synapses.

papers.title: Toward A Whole-Brain Interface Enabled by High-Resolution Surface Electrophysiology.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Presented a multi-subject aggregation approach using high-resolution surface electrophysiology from 70 patients implanted with a conformal thin-film neural interface, creating a functional atlas of the human CNS with over 100,000 electrode deployments. Demonstrated somatotopic organization, canonical frequency-band signatures such as beta suppression and high-gamma increases, and real-time neural decoding for neuroprosthetic control and speech decoding.

papers.title: A Novel Digital Phenotype of Physical Activity: Associations with Heart Rate Fragmentation
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 602 male veterans, Gaussian mixture modeling identified two overlapping physical activity phenotypes, compact-early and diffuse-late, based on accelerometry across six domains. The diffuse-late phenotype was associated with modestly higher heart rate fragmentation (PIP and IALS), suggesting a link between activity timing and neuroautonomic dysregulation.

papers.title: SIGMA: SIgnaling via Golgi Morphology Analysis for pathway-state classification.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduced SIGMA, a framework that classifies active signaling pathways from Golgi morphology using imaging flow cytometry and teacher-student knowledge distillation. Applied to MRC-5 fibroblasts across six conditions, SIGMA achieved 90.02% cell-level accuracy and correctly assigned five of seven structurally unrelated compounds to expected pathway classes.

papers.title: EEG Microstates are Not Associated with Psychotic Symptoms, Neurocognitive Domains or Psychosocial Functioning in Adolescents and Young Adults with Clinical High Risk for Psychosis.
papers.summary: Examined associations between resting-state EEG microstates and psychotic symptoms, neurocognitive domains, and psychosocial functioning in 100 adolescents and young adults at clinical high risk for psychosis. Found no significant correlations, suggesting microstate alterations do not directly reflect the neurobiology of clinical symptoms or functional outcomes.

papers.title: The engagement of layer 6 corticothalamic neurons in somatosensation.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In awake mice, layer 6 corticothalamic (L6CT) neurons in somatosensory cortex robustly encoded the presence versus absence of tactile stimuli but were weak encoders of stimulus strength. During a detection task, their responses strongly reflected whether the animal detected the stimulus and predicted behavioral outcome better than other cortical excitatory neurons.

papers.title: PRNP D178N-129MM prion disease: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease-like cortical ribboning without prominent early insomnia.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 59-year-old woman with PRNP D178N-129MM prion disease presenting with rapidly progressive cognitive-language decline and extensive cortical DWI ribboning without prominent early insomnia. A focused literature review identified six previously reported D178N-129MM cases with prion-compatible cortical or cortical-striatal DWI abnormalities.

papers.title: Complementing Engel Classification: Postoperative Scalp EEG as an Objective Indicator in SEEG-Guided Radiofrequency Thermocoagulation-A Seizure-Onset Pattern-Based Stratified Analysis.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 25 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy treated with SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation, low-voltage fast activity (LVFA)-present seizure-onset patterns were strongly associated with seizure freedom (92.3% vs. 33.3%, p=0.004) and postoperative scalp EEG normalization (87.5% vs. 33.3%, p=0.028). Postoperative EEG normalization complemented Engel classification as an objective outcome indicator.

papers.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Nonlesional Extratemporal Epilepsy Surgery Using Subdural Grid Implantation.
papers.summary: In a retrospective study of 55 patients with nonlesional extratemporal epilepsy who underwent subdural grid-guided surgery, seizure freedom (Engel class I) was achieved in 21.8% at 6 months and 54.5% at 2 years. Improvements over time were not statistically significant, and no statistically significant predictors of outcome were found.

papers.title: The cognitive cost of artificial intelligence on ageing workforce: Analyzing age-related effects on mental workload and task performance in computer-based environment.
papers.summary: In 30 older workers performing computer-based office tasks, AI assistance improved overall task performance but increased neurophysiological and systemic strain, with decreased NASA-TLX workload but reduced HRV and increased frontal, parietal, and occipital beta-alpha ratios. The results suggest AI redistributes rather than eliminates workload, increasing executive verification and visual monitoring demands.

papers.title: Radiosurgical capsulotomy for treatment-resistant obsessive-compulsive disorder through a network neuroscience lens.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines evidence from structural MRI, diffusion imaging, functional connectivity, electrophysiology, and radiobiology to evaluate radiosurgical capsulotomy for treatment-resistant OCD through a network neuroscience lens. The authors conclude that current evidence supports a network-informed research framework but does not establish a validated network mechanism, individualized targeting biomarker, or post-radiosurgery plasticity window, and highlight the need for harmonized longitudinal imaging and dose-volume-connectivity analyses.

papers.title: Neuromonitoring of perioperative microembolization and its association with postoperative stroke after carotid endarterectomy.
papers.summary: In 257 carotid endarterectomy procedures, this study assessed whether perioperative microembolization detected by transcranial Doppler and EEG neuromonitoring can identify patients at risk for postoperative stroke. Postoperative stroke occurred in 7 patients, and exploratory penalized regression showed that higher postoperative microembolic signal counts and an intraoperative burden of ≥10 MES were associated with postoperative stroke, though the authors note these hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation.

papers.title: Neuronal primary cilia are not required for hippocampal circuit function or behavior in adult mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using mouse genetic and behavioral studies, single-cell electrophysiology, and 2-photon imaging, this study tested whether primary cilia are required for hippocampal circuit function or behavior in adult mice. Chronic genetic deletion or acute laser ablation of primary cilia from mature CA1 or CA3 pyramidal neurons did not affect neuronal excitability, basal synaptic transmission, long-term synaptic plasticity, hippocampal-dependent learning and memory, or anxiety-like behaviors, challenging the prevailing view of cilia function in mature hippocampal neurons.

papers.title: Taking a clinical history in adolescents and adults presenting with seizures or epilepsy.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from January 2000 to April 2026, along with landmark studies and ILAE/NICE guidelines, to develop a structured framework for clinical history-taking in adolescents and adults presenting with seizures or epilepsy, integrating the updated 2025 ILAE seizure classification. The authors present a stepwise approach covering event reconstruction, semiology, witness accounts, smartphone videos, triggers, and differential diagnosis, and provide practical diagnostic questionnaires to improve diagnostic accuracy and seizure classification in routine practice.

papers.title: Viral Strategies for In Vivo Optogenetic Stimulation of Purkinje Cell Terminals and Electrophysiological Characterization of Downstream Cerebellar Nuclear Activity in Mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This protocol describes two viral strategies with differing cell-type specificities for in vivo optogenetic control of cerebellar Purkinje cells and electrophysiological characterization of downstream medial deep cerebellar nuclear activity in mice. It details expression of the fast channelrhodopsin ChETA in Purkinje cells to enable light-evoked activation of axonal terminals and demonstrates light-evoked modulation of mDCN neural activity using in vivo extracellular electrophysiology.

papers.title: Single-Channel Electrophysiology Using a Miniaturized Montal-Mueller Planar Lipid Bilayer System for Recording a Synthetic K2P Channel.
papers.summary: The paper presents a miniaturized Montal-Mueller planar lipid bilayer system (BLMchipMM) integrated with a compact amplifier for stable single-channel recordings with reduced reagent consumption. The system was validated by reconstituting a synthetic K2P channel (ancTREK1), which showed a current-voltage relationship in Mg2+-free symmetric K+ solutions with conductance values consistent with TREK1 channels.

papers.title: Pathogenic Mechanisms of Two Novel Variants in the GJB1 Gene.
papers.summary: The study investigated two novel GJB1 variants (c.130dupT and c.124A>G) in eight male patients with CMTX1, revealing distinct pathogenic mechanisms: c.130dupT causes loss of full-length Cx32 expression, while c.124A>G leads to cytoplasmic retention and impaired channel function due to structural constriction and increased electrostatic barrier. These findings expand the genetic spectrum of CMTX1 and provide a basis for precise molecular diagnosis.

papers.title: Human Th17 state classification reveals a selective vulnerability in acylcarnitine metabolism in type 2 diabetes
papers.summary: The authors developed a nanovial-based single-cell ELISA to isolate cytokine-secreting human Th17 cells and define transcriptional signatures of non-pathogenic versus pathogenic Th17 states. Applying these tools with metabolic modeling revealed that Th17np cells predominate in type 2 diabetes and exhibit impaired fatty acid oxidation despite elevated CPT1A, identifying acylcarnitine metabolism as a regulator of Th17 state balance and a selective metabolic vulnerability in type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Case Report: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizures as initial presentation of Lhermitte-Duclos Disease and Cowden Syndrome.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 38-year-old female presenting with bilateral tonic-clonic seizures, leading to a diagnosis of Lhermitte-Duclos disease and Cowden syndrome via 7T MRI and identification of a pathogenic PTEN germline variant. The patient was subsequently diagnosed with ductal carcinoma in situ and thyroid atypia, highlighting the importance of recognizing underlying hereditary cancer syndromes for timely cancer detection.

papers.title: Methodology for identification of depleted metallic uranium and natural metallic uranium by portable gamma spectrometer.
papers.journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
papers.summary: The study developed a portable gamma spectrometry methodology using a NaI(Tl) spectrometer to distinguish depleted metallic uranium (DU) from natural metallic uranium (NU) by analyzing gamma peaks at 92 keV (234Th) and 186 keV (235U). The activity ratio of 235U to 234Th was found to be ≥0.046 for NU and <0.046 for DU, validating the method for real-time, non-destructive uranium isotope identification.

papers.title: Step-by-Step Protocol for Fluorescence-Based Analysis of Uptake in Transporter-Expressing Xenopus laevis Oocytes.
papers.summary: This paper presents a step-by-step protocol for a fluorescence-based uptake assay in Xenopus laevis oocytes using the Arabidopsis thaliana sucrose transporter 1 (SUC1) and its fluorescent substrate esculin. The method enables rapid quantification of transporter activity via a plate reader, eliminating the need for radiolabeled compounds or electrophysiology, and is adaptable to other transporter-substrate pairs.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
